title: Close the machine's finger guard, then press the start button
instruction: Slide the yellow guard all the way across the grey machine, then press the green start button.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); table top z = 0.7475 m. Everything is a rigid matte primitive with friction 1.2 static and 1.0 dynamic unless stated. Machine: grey block 20 x 32 x 8 cm (x, y, z) centred at x 30, y 0, 25 kg in the sim (it stands in for a machine bolted to the bench). Guard: yellow plate 12 x 10 x 3 cm on a slide on the machine's left side at y +12, resting at x 23 (open); it can slide 14 cm along +x, has a light return spring (10 N/m) and viscous damping (20 N s/m), so it springs back to open when released. Start button: green square key 4 x 4 x 1.5 cm on the machine's right side at x 30, y -12, 0.8 cm of travel, 100 N/m return spring. To build it: print the parts, run the guard on a slide with a weak return spring, and bolt the machine down.
scoring: Measured at the end with a ruler and a photo. 0 if the machine moved more than 5 mm. Otherwise: pressing the button in (6.4 mm or more) while the guard is open less than 12 cm scores at most 0.25. 1.0 if the guard is slid at least 12 cm, the button is pressed in at least 6.4 mm while it is, and everything is still for 1 s; 0.75 if both are true but not yet still; 0.5 if the guard is slid at least 12 cm and the button is not pressed; 0.25 if the guard is slid at least 6 cm (and the button is not pressed in at the wrong time); else 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. In the sim the scorer reads the machine pose and the guard and button joints, not the grippers.
fidelity: Approximate. The guard and button are spring-loaded prismatic joints on a 25 kg body. The guard's return spring is only 10 N/m so the arm can hold it closed; there is no latch, so it springs open again when released. The machine is fixed, so it cannot be dragged. The interlock is only in the scorer: nothing physically blocks the button when the guard is open. No contact force cap.
context: Machinists and press operators must close the point-of-operation guard before starting a machine cycle (OSHA 1910.212, O*NET 51-4031.00).
reset_notes: Let the guard spring back to open (x 23) and the button return to rest, and keep the machine at x 30, y 0. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the open-loop demo depends on the exact layout.
